item.title: Vunidogoloa seeks answers over 12-year-old relocation concerns
item.description: Vunidogoloa villagers in Vanua Levu are still waiting for answers on several basic infrastructure and welfare needs, 12 years after the community was relocated from its original coastal site. Former Vunidogoloa headman Sailosi Ramatu raised the concerns during the Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu this evening, saying the community has repeatedly sought Gov
item.content:encoded:
Vunidogoloa villagers in Vanua Levu are still waiting for answers on several basic infrastructure and welfare needs, 12 years after the community was relocated from its original coastal site.

Former Vunidogoloa headman Sailosi Ramatu raised the concerns during the Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu this evening, saying the community has repeatedly sought Government assistance but has received no response on several of the issues.

Vunidogoloa was relocated about 2 kilometres inland from its original site in 2014, with coastal erosion among the factors that contributed to the relocation.

Ramatu says the drainage system at the new site was established during the relocation, but had not been maintained.

He warns that inadequate drainage could lead to further erosion at the new site.

Ramatu also raised concerns about the lack of proper access for elderly residents and people with disabilities, particularly during emergencies.

Insert: Ramatu - We are concerned for the elderly Sept 23

Another concern is the community church, which Ramatu says was supposed to be included in the relocation package.

He says residents had contributed around $260,000 of their own money towards completing the church, despite it having been included in the Government-funded relocation package.

Ramatu adds that the community has no proper ground or playground at the new site, which he describes as important for maintaining traditional practices and providing a safe space for young people.

He says the community had also been waiting for a proper farm road, which is particularly important because many residents now rely on farming for their livelihoods.

Ramatu says the community had been raising the farm road issue with Government for about 12 years but had still not received a response.

He says the community had spent close to $600,000 supporting aspects of the relocation process and is now seeking Government assistance to address the remaining needs.

Ramatu also called for the community hall to be extended so it can serve as an evacuation centre, particularly for elderly residents and people with disabilities.

When reiterated byÂ fijivillage News Director and Fijian Media Association Executive Vijay Narayan Â that there had been no response after 12 years, Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica says previous community relocations had been carried out in an ad hoc manner.

Kamikamica says an Auditor-General's report had highlighted issues with some earlier relocations.

He says Government has since developed a standard operating procedure to improve the way future relocations are carried out.

Kamikamica says relocation was not simply about physically moving people, but also had to consider cultural, spiritual and practical needs.

Minister for Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Management Mosese Bulitavu says some of the issues raised by Ramatu, including farm roads, churches, playgrounds and accessibility for people with disabilities, had not been adequately considered in the original relocation package.

Bulitavu says the Government has since reviewed its standard operating procedure for the relocation trust fund and incorporated lessons from previous relocation projects.

He says existing Government programmes could potentially support footpaths, footbridges and evacuation facilities.

Bulitavu says that failures from the previous governments will be adressed.

item.title: WATCH: Savusavu residents raise climate concerns directly with Kamikamica at FMA Town Hall
item.description: Savusavu residents got the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he attended the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues tonight. The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum was held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu.
item.content:encoded:
Savusavu residents got the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he attended the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues tonight.

The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum was held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu.

The forum, organised by the FMA , gave residents an opportunity to raise concerns about environmental and climate challenges affecting their communities, question Government action and propose practical solutions.

Kamikamica, joined by Minister for NDRMO Mosese Bulitavu, other Government officials and experts from regional agencies were in Savusavu for the PINA Media Summit.

The discussion was moderated by fijivillage News Director Vijay Narayan and Fiji Television Manager News Stella Taoi.

Residents shared their own experiences, including changes they have observed, challenges affecting their livelihoods and solutions they believe should receive greater attention.

Questions around Government responses and the support needed by communities also formed part of the discussion.

The forum was livestreamed across participating media platforms, including fijivillage.

It was held alongside the 8th Pacific Media Summit, hosted by the Fijian Media Association and the Pacific Islands News Association.

The town hall is aimed at bringing community voices into the regional gathering of Pacific journalists and media leaders, while creating a direct platform for public discussion and accountability on climate and environmental issues.

The event is supported by PACMAS and forms part of the Fijian Media Association’s collaborative town hall initiative involving Fiji’s media organisations.

item.title: Rabuka confirms Feb 6th 2027 election deadline remains unchanged
item.description: Vijay Narayan , Rashika Kumar · 23/09/2026 Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Government remains committed to holding the next general elections by 6th February next year, with no legal basis for a one-year extension.
item.content:encoded:
Vijay Narayan , Rashika Kumar · 23/09/2026

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Government remains committed to holding the next general elections by 6th February next year, with no legal basis for a one-year extension.

While responding to questions by fijivillage News in Savusavu, Rabuka confirms thereÂ have been suggestions to extend the deadline for the elections, but it is outside the law.

When questioned about concerns that the constitution process is being rushed, Rabuka says they started talking about the constitution in 2013, when it was decreed into being.

He says everybody were talking about it, and everybody who had spoken about it should have come forward during the consultation.

Rabuka adds the result of the consultation is what they are now taking through Parliament.

He also says that the recommendations in the Constitution Review Commission's report are not the final proposed amendments that will go before Parliament.

He says a Cabinet sub-committee has been deliberating on the Commission's proposed amendments over the past two weeks and making changes.

The Prime Minister says those changes will be the ones that make their way to Parliament. Click here to find the Constitution Review Commission report.

item.title: Sigatoka couple turns family garage operation into growing export business
item.description: 31-year-old Vinesh Varun Sharma and his wife Vandhana started Vinesh Export in 2023, initially converting their garage into a makeshift packhouse as they worked to get the business off the ground. The couple now source fruits, vegetables and root crops from farmers in Sigatoka, other parts of the Western Division and Central Viti Levu.
item.content:encoded:
31-year-old Vinesh Varun Sharma and his wife Vandhana started Vinesh Export in 2023, initially converting their garage into a makeshift packhouse as they worked to get the business off the ground.

The couple now source fruits, vegetables and root crops from farmers in Sigatoka, other parts of the Western Division and Central Viti Levu.

Produce including eggplant, pawpaw, okra, chillies, ginger, cassava and dalo is exported to New Zealand, while pearl guava is sent to Japan.

Sharma says the business exported 43,560 kilograms of produce in 2024, earning $348,480.

A year later, exports had increased to 81,100 kilograms, with income rising to $648,800.

Sharma says the money earned is reinvested into the business to help it continue growing.

The business is also providing another market for local farmers, collecting vegetables from them every Thursday and Saturday for export.

As the operation expanded, Vinesh Export received support through the Ministry of Agriculture's Commercial Agriculture Development Programme, which provided a packhouse and cooler valued at $87,398.

The facilities have allowed the family to handle larger volumes of produce while maintaining the quality required for export.

Vinesh Export currently employs five full-time and 10 casual workers.

However, expanding the business has also brought challenges.

The company currently has one three-tonne truck to transport produce to the airport and sometimes has to make two trips when export orders are high.

Sharma says maintaining the quality of produce is another important part of the operation, as products that do not meet export standards cannot be sent overseas.

Despite these challenges, the family plans to continue expanding the business and creating more opportunities for farmers to supply produce for overseas markets.

For Sharma and Vandhana, the business has come a long way from the makeshift packhouse in their family garage, and they are now focused on expanding the operation further.

item.title: 21-year-old content creator Maharaj becomes two-time world record holder
item.description: 21-year-old Fijian content creator Anush Maharaj is now a two-time Guinness World Record holder after being recognised for identifying the most countries in 30 seconds. Maharaj, also known as The Mystic and originally from Labasa, secured the record on 21st of this month following a verification process that took almost seven months.
item.content:encoded:
21-year-old Fijian content creator Anush Maharaj is now a two-time Guinness World Record holder after being recognised for identifying the most countries in 30 seconds.

Maharaj, also known as The Mystic and originally from Labasa, secured the record on 21st of this month following a verification process that took almost seven months.

Maharaj says he was happy to receive confirmation of his second world record and is proud to have represented Fiji on a global stage.

He says his latest record is different from his first achievement because it is a completely new title, with no previous record holder.

Maharaj previously broke the world record for identifying the most company logos in 30 seconds after identifying 60 logos.

He says the previous record was held by India, making his first achievement a record he surpassed, while his latest achievement is the first record of its kind and is currently held by Fiji.

Maharaj says the process of securing his latest record took months because applicants have to wait for guidelines, complete the record attempt and submit the required evidence before it can be verified.

He says he was motivated to pursue the records by his goal of building a career in content creation.

Maharaj is a content creator who posts vlogs on TikTok, and says his dream is to become one of the biggest content creators in Fiji.

He says he decided to pursue another world record after his first achievement did not result in the opportunities he had hoped for.

Maharaj says although it was heartbreaking at the time, he decided to continue working towards his goal and spent months preparing for his second record.

He hopes his latest achievement will open up opportunities and help him build a career through content creation.

Maharaj also reflected on his experience with cyberbullying and says young people should understand that hate and criticism can come with gaining popularity on social media.

He says people should not allow negative comments to distract them from their goals and should instead focus on what they are trying to achieve.

Maharaj says he does not yet have a definite plan for another world record but has not ruled out attempting a third record if an opportunity arises.

His message to young people is to pursue their dreams, believe in themselves and not allow people who doubt them to stop them.

Maharaj says he wants to continue creating content and hopes his achievements can help show that Fijians can gain international recognition through their talents and determination.
